description:
## Purpose
Notes item, kept blocked so it cannot be claimed. It holds the owner's decisions and the order of the steps. It closes when every step is done, dropped with the owner's reason, or blocked on a named owner gate.

## Problem
`benchbox run` has no timeout. Time bounds are scattered: UAT kills each cell from outside; dsqgen, qgen and tool compilation have hard-coded limits; throughput streams stop at 3600 or 7200 seconds; plan capture abandons a thread; engines each have their own setting; `utils/timeout_manager.py`, `ResourceLimitsConfig` and three config keys hold timers nothing enforces. The runner has no way to stop a run except for throughput streams.

## Owner's request
"We should have a generalized run timeout (e.g. `--timeout SECONDS`) that applies to any type of run; not jsut data generation but also benchmark executions." "We do need to **ALLOW** a user to specify a datagen timeout even though we MUST NOT enforce a default timeout."

## Settled semantics (owner, choice dialog, 2026-11-20)
- Name: `--timeout SECONDS`, whole seconds, on `run`, `run-official` and `datagen`; `timeout_seconds` in the MCP run tool; `execution.timeout_seconds` in the config file. 0 means no limit (owner: "0 means no limit, matching the existing settings; it lets a command line switch off a limit set in the config file. Negative and fractional values are usage errors.").
- Python: "`timeout_seconds=` on both documented calls [`benchmark.generate_data()` and `adapter.run_benchmark()`]. Each call gets its own clock ... In Python a timeout raises `RunTimeoutError`; there is no hard exit of the caller's process, and the docs say so."
- No run limit unless the user sets one. (Container start-up, health-check and credential limits, the binary `-h` probes and plan capture's own limit are outside this and stay.)
- Scope: one clock for the whole invocation, generate, load and execute together; narrower settings stay as tighter limits inside it.
- At the limit: BenchBox asks everything to stop (cancels where it can, kills generator processes). If the run has not stopped after a fixed 30-second grace, it writes what it has and exits. The hard bound is the limit plus 30 seconds.
- Marker: "a new status value `timed_out` in `summary.validation`, plus a new optional key `execution.timeout` holding `timeout_seconds`, `phase` and `query_id`." A timed-out result can never be official, published, submitted or ranked.
- Exit code 124.

## Delivery
Owner: "five pull requests, one per step, each merged before the next starts. Nothing is stacked. I work them in order without stopping between them unless a gate fails." Then, on the size of step 1: "split step 1 into two pull requests, merged in order ... Six pull requests in all." ('I' is the agent.)

## Order (each needs the one before)
1a. tpc-generation-no-default-timeout-optional-user-timeout-20261120
1b. run-timeout-generators-and-partial-data-20261120
2. run-timeout-execution-phases-20261120
3. run-timeout-remote-cleanup-20261120
4. run-timeout-uat-cells-20261120
5. run-timeout-remove-unused-timers-20261120
Then tpc-generation-duration-estimate-20261120.

## Other decisions
- No new CI check against hard-coded timeouts. Container start-up, health-check and credential literals stay.
- Fixed generation limits: qgen and compile limits removed; the 5 and 15 second `-h` probes stay.
- Execution defaults removed; unenforced config keys removed in step 5.
- UAT: `timed-out` for a cell BenchBox stopped, `hung` for one the runner killed.
- Cloud cleanup verified with stubs only, with a warning; no live cloud runs.

## Delivery (owner, 2026-11-21): feature batches; this replaces "one pull request per step"
One session delivers all six remaining items. A batch has one integration branch, members built by subagents, and one final pull request.
1. Precondition: step 1a (PR #4423) merged and its item finished.
2. Batch `run-timeout-core`: run-timeout-generators-and-partial-data-20261120; run-timeout-execution-phases-20261120; run-timeout-remote-cleanup-20261120 (depends on the execution-phases member). The TPC-DI effort waits for this batch to merge.
3. Serial in benchbox-site: documentation for `--timeout` (run, datagen, MCP and configuration pages), on the branch the site's rule names for unreleased features.
4. Batch `run-timeout-harness`: run-timeout-uat-cells-20261120; run-timeout-remove-unused-timers-20261120.
5. Serial: tpc-generation-duration-estimate-20261120.

## Decisions of 2026-11-21 (choice dialog)
- Grouping: two batches as above, then the estimate alone. At most 2 member subagents implement at once. If a batch would exceed the review bot's size limit, the leader splits it in the same order and tells the owner afterwards. A pull request refused twice at arming stops that batch.
- Step 2 timing proof: "Keep the stop: more than 2% apart blocks the batch and the table comes to me."
- Removed stream defaults: "Set the old value explicitly in that configuration and list each place in the pull request. No stop."
- Step 3 warning, cleanup implemented: "A run time limit is set. If the run times out, BenchBox will try to cancel the work it started on {platform}. This cleanup has not been checked against the live service, so work may keep running and billing." Not implemented: "A run time limit is set. If the run times out, work BenchBox started on {platform} may keep running and billing: BenchBox cannot cancel it on this platform."
- Step 5 removed-key message: "`{key}` is no longer used and has no effect. Use `execution.timeout_seconds` to limit a run."
- Other new names and messages: "No stop: follow existing conventions and list each in the pull request."
- Plan capture keeps its own 30-second default. Time spent waiting for the host lock does not count toward the limit; the docs say so.
- Estimate: "Approve the runs now, and let the session commit the measured figures; the table is in the pull request and the final report. No stop." Texts: "Rough estimate: generation will take about {estimate} (measured on {host_class} at scale {scales}{extrapolated_note})." and "The run limit of {limit} seconds is shorter than the estimated generation time of about {estimate}."
- Site documentation for `--timeout` is included, as step 3 above.
- Stops that remain: the step 2 timing gate; a pull request the review bot marks too large after a split; a pull request refused twice; a name or key in step 5 that turns out to have a real caller; a measurement run refused admission or breaching the disk floor; any Decision gate that says stop.

## Gates that stop at the owner
- Any pull request the review bot marks too large to review.
- Step 2: medians more than 2% apart; any explicit value a test tier or UAT config turns out to need.
- (Settled 2026-11-21: the step 3 warning, the step 5 message, the estimate's figures and texts; see the decisions above.)
- (Settled 2026-11-21: plan capture keeps its default; waiting for the host lock does not count toward the limit.)

## Guardrails (owner, 2026-11-20)
The agent never posts a stand-in review, closes and reopens a pull request to restart CI, uses `--no-verify`, force-pushes, rewrites an author, or deletes anything under `~/Developer/benchmark_runs`. Arming: `make pr-arm` once; one more attempt only when the refusal named a cause, the agent reported it and the cause is cleared; never a third without asking; `make pr-rerun` at most once and only for a job that never ran or was cancelled by the runner, never for a test that failed. Review threads: reply, and resolve only after the bot's review of the new head does not raise the finding again. Subagents implement batch members and serial items under the delivery plan on run-timeout-plan-20261120 (owner, 2026-11-21); a batch member makes no tracker write, opens no pull request and stops at a landing report. A limit, default, threshold, status token, message or label text the owner has chosen is used verbatim (see run-timeout-plan-20261120). Any other new name or message follows existing BenchBox conventions and is listed in the pull request (owner, 2026-11-21: no stop for these). No file edit by script; use the edit tool. Do not edit a pull request description while its CI is starting; post a comment. A blocked step stops this item; no workaround. No live cloud run. Heavy work only through `make heavy-run`.
